settings.heading: Is workplace drug and alcohol testing legal in Australia?
settings.text: Workplace testing can be lawful when it is reasonable, connected to genuine workplace risk and supported by applicable employment arrangements, consultation and a clearly communicated policy. Requirements vary by workplace and jurisdiction, so organisations should obtain advice for their circumstances.

settings.heading: Does every employee need to be tested?
settings.text: Not necessarily. The scope should be risk-based and defined in policy. Some organisations include the whole workforce; others focus on safety-sensitive roles, company drivers, specific locations or clearly defined testing triggers.

settings.heading: How should we handle a non-negative result?
settings.text: A non-negative screening result is not the same as a confirmed positive. Follow the documented chain-of-custody, confirmation, confidential review and response process set out in your workplace policy.

settings.heading: Can prescribed medication be considered?
settings.text: Yes. Your program should include a confidential declaration and review pathway so prescribed medication can be assessed appropriately without treating a screening result as a final determination.

settings.heading: Can one program cover multiple offices and sites?
settings.text: Yes. Equipment, procedures, training, calibration and reporting can be standardised across locations while allowing for genuine differences in roles, risks and operating hours.
